Let me carefully design the implementation.

We need robust JSON parsing with duplicate key rejection, non-finite numbers, invalid UTF-8, trailing JSON. Python's json module by default allows NaN/Infinity (parse_constant), can use object_pairs_hook to detect duplicate keys. Need reject invalid UTF-8: read stdin bytes and decode strict. Also reject duplicate keys in nested objects.

Root exactly keys version, traces. All objects exactly listed keys. Need validate every structural aspect: unknown keys, wrong types, out-of-domain, structural limits.

Important: "Reject duplicate object keys, non-finite numbers, invalid UTF-8, trailing JSON, unknown keys, wrong types, out-of-domain values and violated structural limits." We reject any JSON with duplicate keys anywhere, including obviously invalid deeper objects. Also nested depth attack: json decoder may recurse; Python's C scanner raises RecursionError for deep nesting maybe. Need catch exceptions. Deeply nested JSON not matching grammar invalid, not crash. Set recursion limit? The json C parser may hit recursion limit -> RecursionError caught. Better set sys.setrecursionlimit maybe high? Attack with huge depth could cause stack overflow killed? Python's C parser respects recursion limit. We can keep default or set e.g. 10000. Inputs up to 16MiB; a million-deep array could produce RecursionError. Catch BaseException? MemoryError too. We must output INVALID_INPUT on invalid input. Catch (ValueError, RecursionError, MemoryError, OverflowError) around parsing, but don't catch KeyboardInterrupt etc. Probably catch Exception broadly around parse.

Integers: JSON number must be integer, never float. In Python json parses "1" as int, "1.0" as float, "1e3" as float. Reject floats. Booleans are subclass of int, so explicit check type(x) is int. Numeric values are JSON integers, never booleans. Use type(v) is int.

Version must == 1.

Trace IDs unique. regex.

Counts limits across request: traces <=32, events <=20000, packets <=20000, frames <=60000, decoded data <=2MiB (sum of decoded bytes over all CRYPTO/STREAM frames, including packets that will be discarded? "These counts include packets that will be discarded." I think total across input). Request at most 16MiB bytes. Note decoded frame data total 2MiB. HEX max 2048 bytes each. Also at most 16 packets per datagram, 0..64 frames.

Need distinguish structural limits: e.g., datagram packets 1..16, frames 0..64. "at most 16 packets"; grammar says 1..16. So reject 0 packets or >16. Root traces <=32. Events per trace <=20000? Packet counts include packets in events. Frames count. Decoded data bytes sum of len(bytes.fromhex(data_hex)) for CRYPTO/STREAM. Check <= 2*1024*1024.

RANGES for config: array max 32 pairs, each pair length exactly 2 integers 0..2^62-1, low<=high, ascend by low, disjoint and nonadjacent. "ascend by low, and be disjoint and nonadjacent." So strictly increasing lows, and previous high +1 < next low (nonadjacent means next low > prev high+1). Empty allowed.

Frame ACK ranges same endpoint and length domains (max 32 pairs? The grammar says "A frame's ACK ranges use the same endpoint and length domains" - so at most 32 pairs) but may be empty, reversed, overlapping, adjacent or unsorted: those are protocol errors, as specified below (FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR). Structural validation only checks domain: array <=32 pairs, each pair two ints in range. Whether empty allowed at input grammar level: yes, then protocol error. So parse ranges generically (<=32, each [low, high] ints in 0..2^62-1) and then semantic config validation or ACK preflight.

Note RANGES structural: array of at most 32 pairs, pair exactly length 2. If a frame ACK has >32 pairs, structural invalid input.

EVENT: exactly keys per op. All t in domain, nondecreasing within trace. t integer 0..1e12. "exactly one of" - validate op string exactly.

key event exactly t,op,level,action. levels I,H,Z,A. action install/discard.
tick exactly t,op.
datagram exactly t,op,bytes,packets. bytes int 0..65535. packets 1..16. Each packet exactly keys level,pn,auth,frames. level label valid; pn int 0..2^62-1; auth bool; frames array 0..64. Each frame validate as per type exact keys, fields.

Frame types:
PADDING: exact {"type"}
PING exact
ACK: {"type","ranges"} ranges structural <=32 pairs ints.
CRYPTO: type, offset N, data_hex HEX. offset 0..2^62-1. HEX lowercase hex only, even length, <=2048 bytes (len string <=4096), length even. Empty allowed.
STREAM: type,id,offset,data_hex,fin. id 0..2^62-1, offset same, fin bool.
RESET_STREAM: type,id,final_size N.
STOP_SENDING: type,id.
CLOSE: type,app bool,code N (code 0..2^62-1 presumably N domain).
HANDSHAKE_DONE: type only.
UNKNOWN: type only.

Unknown frame names invalid input: type must one of listed.

State per trace:
- keys: dict I,H,Z,A -> absent/live/discarded. Initial I live, H absent, A absent, Z live if early else absent.
- connection: state open/closed/idle; code; at_ms; source (event/packet/frame); peer_code; last_activity_ms=0.
- PN sets: per space. I, H, Application (shared Z/A). Successful accepted packets add pn.
- pending queue: list of queued packets with original event/packet indices, arrival time (event t), and packet data. At most buffer_packets per trace. Pending packets across levels; when installing a key, process its pending packets (matching level) in original arrival order before next event. However there may be pending packets for other levels; queue slots consumed.

Important: pending packets can be dropped at key event time as KEYS_DISCARDED when discard key. And already pending dropped at termination as CONNECTION_CLOSED at termination time.
